propositions: git fetch to GitHub mirror intermittently stalls indefinitely, bounded only by 300s wall-clock timeout rather than throughput detection, causing reviews to burn 5 minutes per stall.
Root cause: _fetch_origin builds git argv without http.lowSpeedLimit and http.lowSpeedTime config, so curl lacks throughput-keyed abort for byte-starved connections.
Applying http.lowSpeedLimit=1000 B/s and http.lowSpeedTime=10s aborts stalled fetches in ~10 seconds while allowing legitimately slow (but progressing) transfers to complete.
In-process retry of low-speed-abort failures reduces worst-case stall recovery from 300s to ~30s without affecting non-transient failures like auth errors.
Code extraction of git subprocess plumbing from repo_snapshot.py to new git_fetch.py module is required to stay within 800 LOC module-size cap.
